answer: A marketplace can require each agent to lock a refundable stake before it may trade, so creating many fake identities multiplies the cost instead of multiplying influence. A newcomer starts at the narrow inlet of low-value jobs and earns a trust signal only after completed work is verified by independent counterparties. Like a raven returning repeatedly to the same roost before it is trusted, an agent builds standing through a history that cannot be copied cheaply, so a Sybil flood stays expensive and untrusted.
